principles: A check must be bound to the property it guarantees, not to a snapshot of the population it once saw.
A guard that cannot fail, or that never runs, is not protection - it is a confident success line.
An exclusion is a decision and must carry a reason; silent absence is indistinguishable from an oversight.
Prove a guard bites before trusting it; an unobserved bite is a claim, not evidence.
Do not narrow a derivation with a pattern that can itself go stale.
drivers: The blindness has already manifested 18 times; 15 harnesses are executed by no automated path and the symptom is silence, not failure.
The instrument meant to report this is itself unregistered, so it never runs under lattice validate.
A working reference implementation exists in the same directory, so the corrected shape is mechanical rather than novel.
Measured cost of running everything is well under a minute, so the historical runtime objection is void.

options.name: A - append the missing entries to the existing hardcoded lists
cons: Leaves the instrument blind to the next addition, which IS the defect
Repeats the exact mistake being fixed
Provides no signal when someone adds a harness and forgets

options.name: B - derive both populations from disk, require registered-or-excluded-with-reason, and register the guard itself
pros: Binds the check to the property rather than a snapshot
Reference implementation already exists and its bite was proven in both directions
Covers the tests/red population that currently has no guard at all
A future addition fails loudly instead of slipping through
cons: Must resist narrowing the enumeration with a name pattern, which would silently recreate the defect
Requires deciding one guard versus two with disjoint declared populations
Adds commands to lattice validate, so the runtime budget must be re-measured rather than assumed

options.name: C - delete the unreached harnesses instead of registering them
cons: Destroys proof artifacts from earlier stories that were written as evidence and still pass
Confuses 'nobody runs it' with 'it has no value'
Would discard the protected invariance harness's siblings without any analysis of what they cover

chosen: B - derive both populations from disk, require registered-or-excluded-with-reason, and register the guard itself
rationale: Option A treats the symptom and leaves the instrument blind, which is precisely the defect. Option C mistakes 'unrun' for 'worthless' and would destroy evidence from earlier stories that still passes. B is the only option that changes what the check is bound to, and its main risk is well understood and cheap to guard against: the enumeration must not be narrowed by a name pattern.

preMortem.scenario: The new guard mirrors chk007's narrow prefix regex and a future differently-prefixed harness lands outside its population.
preMortem.trigger: Copying the reference implementation literally, including /^red-b2aa7-.*\.mjs$/, because it is the working example.
preMortem.consequence: The story ships, the defect is reproduced one prefix over, and the next omission is silent again - with a passing guard as false assurance.
preMortem.mitigation: The constraint is recorded in understanding and repeated in plan.md as a hard requirement: enumerate the directory unfiltered. The RED artifact must include a differently-prefixed newcomer, so a narrowed derivation fails the story's own test.

preMortem.scenario: The two silent pre-fix receipts get registered rather than excluded.
preMortem.trigger: A fresh implementer sees 18 unregistered files and registers all 18 uniformly.
preMortem.consequence: Two commands that pass forever while asserting nothing enter the regression suite - the exact vacuous coverage this story exists to remove, self-inflicted at the last step.
preMortem.mitigation: The reasoning is carried inside CHK-003's own context rather than left to be rediscovered, and the acceptance requires each exclusion to carry a machine-checked reason.

preMortem.scenario: The guard is built and proven, but is itself left unregistered.
preMortem.trigger: Focusing on the population and forgetting the instrument, exactly as the current state arose.
preMortem.consequence: A correct guard that never runs - the present failure, rebuilt.
preMortem.mitigation: The guard must include itself in its own population with no self-exception, so an unregistered guard fails its own check.

preMortem.scenario: Registering everything pushes lattice validate past a timeout on a loaded host.
preMortem.trigger: Trusting the measured 31-40s band instead of re-measuring after registration.
preMortem.consequence: A green story that makes validate flaky for everyone else.
preMortem.mitigation: Re-measure after registering and record the number; if any harness is slow, decide its timeoutMs deliberately rather than inheriting a default.
